<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

payload.resultSummary:
Probe complete. Findings for the requested scope:

## Representative commands and exact outputs

Format: `is_valid_domain is_valid_label is_ascii_domain is_idn_domain` (one per line in the real output).

- `test4_executable` (no arg) and `test4_executable example.com` → `1 1 1 0`
- `test4_executable EXAMPLE.COM` → `1 1 1 0`
- `test4_executable ExAmPlE.CoM` → `1 1 1 0`

Full printable-ASCII sweep, each char `c` embedded as `a<c>b.com` (codes 32–126, i.e. space, `!"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\]^_`{|}~`, digits, both letter cases):

- Every single code 32–126 → `1 1 1 0`, no exceptions. Notably:
  - `a b.com` (space) → `1 1 1 0`
  - `a!b.com`, `a"b.com`, `a~b.com`, `a|b.com` → `1 1 1 0`
  - `a.b.com` (dot just splits into more labels) → `1 1 1 0`

Position/edge contrast probes (outside strict sweep, for rule inference):

- `-ab.com`, `ab-.com`, `.ab.com`, `ab.com.`, `a..b.com`, `-`, `.`, `..`, ` ` (single space) → all `1 1 1 0`
- `""` (empty string) → `0 0 1 0`
- `a<TAB>b.com`, `a<DEL 0x7F>b.com` → `1 1 1 0`
- `a<0x80>b.com` → `1 1 0 1`

## Inferred rules for this scope

- **ASCII case behavior:** fully case-insensitive. Uppercase, lowercase, and mixed case in any label (including TLD) all validate identically (`1 1 1 0`); case alone never triggers `is_idn_domain`.
- **Printable sweep:** `is_valid_domain` / `is_valid_label` impose no character-class restriction at all within this scope — every printable ASCII byte (0x20–0x7E), including space, punctuation, and shell metacharacters, is accepted when embedded in a label, and also at label edges (leading/trailing `-`, `.`, empty labels from `..`). Even control bytes (TAB, DEL) pass.
- `is_valid_domain`/`is_valid_label` appear to reduce to "input is non-empty" in this scope (only `""` yields `0 0`).
- `is_ascii_domain` = 1 iff all bytes are ≤ 0x7F (true even for the empty string).
- `is_idn_domain` = 1 iff any byte ≥ 0x80 is present; it is mutually exclusive with `is_ascii_domain` here and unaffected by ASCII case or punctuation.

For a Rust port: in this scope, `is_valid_domain`/`is_valid_label` = `!s.is_empty()`, `is_ascii_domain` = `s.is_ascii()`, `is_idn_domain` = `s.bytes().any(|b| b >= 0x80)`. Caveat: length limits (63/253) and UTF-8/IDNA details of non-ASCII inputs were out of scope and not probed.

| Input | Output (4 lines) |
|---|---|
| *(no arg)* / `example.com` / `abc` / `123.com` | `1 1 1 0` |
| `example-.com`, `-example.com`, `ex-ample.com`, `a-b-c.com` | `1 1 1 0` |

| `exam/ple.com`, `exam:ple.com`, `exam@ple.com` | `1 1 1 0` |
| `exam[ple.com`, `exam]ple.com`, `exam"ple.com`, `exam'ple.com`, `exam\ple.com` | `1 1 1 0` |
| `exam+ple.com`, `exam=ple.com`, `exam,ple.com`, `exam;ple.com` | `1 1 1 0` |
| `a b.com`, `exa mple`, tab / `\x01` / `\x7f` embedded, ` ` (space only) | `1 1 1 0` |
| `.`, `..`, `example.com.`, `.example.com`, `ex..ample.com` | `1 1 1 0` |
| `EXAMPLE.COM`, `xn--nxasmq6b.example`, `xn--` | `1 1 1 0` |
| `""` (empty string) | `0 0 1 0` |
| `bücher.de`, `münchen`, `例え.jp`, `💩.la`, `exäm ple.com` | `1 1 0 1` |
| raw invalid UTF-8 bytes (`a\xffb.com`, `a\x80b`) | `1 1 0 1` |

### Inferred rules (within this ASCII-punctuation scope)

The validators are extremely permissive — none of the probed ASCII punctuation (hyphen in any position, underscore, slash, colon, at-sign, brackets, quotes, backslash, plus, equals, comma, semicolon, space, control chars) nor dot-structure anomalies (leading/trailing/consecutive dots) cause a failure:

- **`is_valid_domain(s)`** = `1` iff `s` is non-empty. No character set, hyphen-position, dot-structure, or label-content restriction observed.
- **`is_valid_label(s)`** = identical behavior: `1` iff `s` is non-empty. It is applied to the whole input string and never disagreed with `is_valid_domain` in any probe.
- **`is_ascii_domain(s)`** = `1` iff every byte of `s` is `< 0x80` (pure byte check; vacuously `1` for empty string). Uppercase, digits, punctuation, control chars, DEL all count as ASCII.
- **`is_idn_domain(s)`** = `1` iff at least one byte of `s` is `>= 0x80`. No UTF-8 validity check — raw `0xFF`/`0x80` bytes count as IDN. It is exactly the negation of `is_ascii_domain` for non-empty inputs; punycode `xn--` prefixes are irrelevant since they're pure ASCII.

**Rust port sketch for this scope:**
```rust
let valid = !s.is_empty();
println!("{}", valid as u8);              // is_valid_domain
println!("{}", valid as u8);              // is_valid_label
println!("{}", s.bytes().all(|b| b < 0x80) as u8); // is_ascii_domain
println!("{}", s.bytes().any(|b| b >= 0x80) as u8); // is_idn_domain
```

**Caveat:** this covers only the requested ASCII-punctuation scope (plus minimal non-ASCII contrast cases to characterize `is_ascii_domain`/`is_idn_domain`). Whether `is_valid_domain`/`is_valid_label` ever return `0` for a non-empty string (e.g., length limits >253/63 chars) was not probed and would need a separate length-focused pass. Note also: use byte-level checks in Rust, not `str::is_ascii()` on potentially invalid UTF-8 CLI input — the executable accepts and classifies invalid UTF-8 bytes.

## Findings

All probing was black-box (executable only). Output order: `is_valid_domain`, `is_valid_label`, `is_ascii_domain`, `is_idn_domain`.

### Representative probes

**Dot / structural extremes** — all produce `1 1 1 0`:
- `"."`, `".."`, `"..."`, `"...."` (dot-only strings)
- `".a"`, `"a."`, `"a..b"`, `"a.b.c"` (leading/trailing/consecutive dots, empty labels)
- No structure is validated at all: dots are treated as ordinary bytes.

**Null-like textual strings** — all `1 1 1 0`:
- `"null"`, `"NULL"`, `"(null)"`, `"nil"`, `"none"`, `"\0"`, `"\x00"`, `" "`, `"  "`, tab/newline-embedded strings
- No special-casing of null-like literals or whitespace/control chars.

**Empty string** `""` → `0 0 1 0` (only failing case for domain/label besides length).

**Length boundaries (single label = whole domain):**

| input | output |
|---|---|
| 63 bytes | `1 1 1 0` |
| 64 bytes | `1 0 1 0` |
| 255 bytes | `1 0 1 0` |
| 256 bytes | `0 0 1 0` |

**Multi-label domains** — `is_valid_domain` ignores the 63-byte label cap:
- `a×64 . a×63` (128 bytes) → `1 0 1 0`
- `a×100 . a×100` (201 bytes) → `1 0 1 0`
- `a×63 . a×63 . a×63 . a×63` (255 bytes) → `1 0 1 0`
- same + `.a` (257 bytes) → `0 0 1 0`

**Unicode:**
- `"münchen.de"`, `"日本語.jp"`, `"é"`, `"☃.net"` → `1 1 0 1`
- `"xn--bcher-kva.ch"` (punycode) → `1 1 1 0` — `xn--` does **not** count as IDN
- 63 **bytes** of `é` → label valid; 64 bytes → `1 0 0 1` (limit is byte-based, and even truncated/invalid UTF-8 passes)
- `"a\x7Fb"` → ascii=1, idn=0; `"a\x80b"` → ascii=0, idn=1

### Inferred rules (byte-length based, `len` = UTF-8 byte count of the argument)

- `is_valid_domain(s)` = `1 <= len(s) <= 255`. Nothing else checked — no label-length, character, dot-position, or dot-count rules.
- `is_valid_label(s)` = `1 <= len(s) <= 63`. No content checks (dots and arbitrary bytes allowed).
- `is_ascii_domain(s)` = every byte `< 0x80` (vacuously true for `""`; DEL `0x7F` counts as ASCII).
- `is_idn_domain(s)` = at least one byte `>= 0x80` (exact complement of ascii; punycode `xn--` prefixes are irrelevant since they're pure ASCII).

In Rust: operate on `s.as_bytes()` / `s.len()` (byte length), never `.chars().count()`.

## Findings

**CLI protocol**
- `./test4_executable` → uses default `"example.com"` → output `1 1 1 0`
- One arg → that arg is tested.
- Multiple args → **only `argv[1]` is used**; extra args silently ignored (`"" example.com` → `0 0 1 0`, i.e. the empty first arg wins).
- Empty-string arg is accepted and processed (no error).
- Flag-like args (`-h`, `--help`, `--version`) are **treated as plain domain strings**, not parsed as options.
- Output: exactly 4 lines, each `0` or `1`, `\n`-terminated, nothing else. Exact bytes for default: `31 0a 31 0a 31 0a 30 0a` (8 bytes). Order: `is_valid_domain`, `is_valid_label`, `is_ascii_domain`, `is_idn_domain`.
- Exit code is always `0`; stderr always empty.

**Representative probes** (output columns = domain label ascii idn):

| input | out | note |
|---|---|---|
| *(none)*, `google.com`, `A.COM`, `1.2.3.4`, `a.b`, `a b.com`, `::1`, `@#$%`, `a..b`, `.com`, `-a.com` | `1 1 1 0` | extremely permissive: any ASCII punctuation/space accepted |
| `""` | `0 0 1 0` | empty fails domain & label; ascii vacuously true |
| 63 chars | `1 1 1 0` | label max boundary |
| 64 chars | `1 0 1 0` | label too long, domain still ok |
| 255 bytes | `1 0 1 0` | domain max boundary |
| 256 bytes | `0 0 1 0` | domain too long |
| `bücher.de`, `例子.cn`, `ü` | `1 1 0 1` | any non-ASCII byte → idn |
| `a\xffb` (invalid UTF-8), `\x80` | `1 1 0 1` | byte-level check, no UTF-8 validation |
| `xn--bcher-kva.ch`, `xn--` | `1 1 1 0` | punycode prefix NOT treated as IDN |
| 63×`ü` (126 bytes) | `1 0 0 1` | length counted in **bytes**, not codepoints |

**Inferred rules** (pure byte-level, no character-class validation):
- `is_valid_domain(s)` = `1 ≤ len_bytes(s) ≤ 255`
- `is_valid_label(s)` = `1 ≤ len_bytes(s) ≤ 63` (applied to the whole argument string, not per-dot-segment — a 250-byte multi-label domain still gave `label=0`)
- `is_ascii_domain(s)` = all bytes `< 0x80` (true for empty string)
- `is_idn_domain(s)` = any byte `≥ 0x80` (i.e. `!is_ascii_domain`, including invalid-UTF-8 bytes; punycode `xn--` ASCII strings are not IDN)

**Rust port sketch** for this scope:
```rust
fn main() {
    let arg = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "example.com".to_string());
    // note: args() panics on invalid UTF-8; use args_os + OsStr bytes if raw-byte fidelity is needed
    let b = arg.as_bytes();
    let n = b.len();
    println!("{}", (n >= 1 && n <= 255) as u8);
    println!("{}", (n >= 1 && n <= 63) as u8);
    println!("{}", b.iter().all(|&c| c < 0x80) as u8);
    println!("{}", b.iter().any(|&c| c >= 0x80) as u8);
}
```
One caveat for the port: `std::env::args()` panics on non-UTF-8 argv; since the binary accepts raw high bytes (`\xff`) fine, the Rust port should use `std::env::args_os()` with `OsStrExt::as_bytes()` on Unix to match exactly.

Ran `/workspace/dataset/test4_executable <arg>` only (no source inspection). Output lines in order: `is_valid_domain`, `is_valid_label`, `is_ascii_domain`, `is_idn_domain`.

## Representative probes (input → 4-line output)

Punycode / `xn--` labels — **nothing punycode-specific is ever checked**:

| input | output | note |
|---|---|---|
| `xn--bcher-kva.ch` | `1 1 1 0` | valid punycode |

| `xn--abc`, `xn--a!`, `xn---`, `xn--.com` | `1 1 1 0` | garbage/undecodable punycode all pass |

| `.`, `..`, `.com`, `com.`, `a..b` | `1 1 1 0` (empty labels, leading/trailing dots fine) |
| `a b.com`, `a_b.com`, `a/b`, `a:b`, `a!.com`, `" "`, real tab/newline | `1 1 1 0` (any ASCII byte allowed) |

Mixed ASCII / non-ASCII:

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `bücher.de`, `exämple.com`, `日本語.jp`, `😀.com`, `ｅｘａｍｐｌｅ.com` | `1 1 0 1` |
| `bücher.xn--fiqs8s`, `xn--bcher-kva.中国`, `xn--abc.ü.com` | `1 1 0 1` |
| raw invalid UTF-8 bytes (`a\xffb.com`, lone `\x80`) | `1 1 0 1` |

Length boundaries (the only validators that ever say `0`):

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `""` (empty) | `0 0 1 0` |
| 63-byte string / 64-byte string | `1 1 1 0` / `1 0 1 0` |
| `a`*60 + `.com` (64 bytes total) | `1 0 1 0` (label check counts whole string's bytes) |
| 31×`ü` (62 B) / 32×`ü` (64 B) | `1 1 0 1` / `1 0 0 1` (byte-based, not char-based) |
| 255-byte / 256-byte domain | `1 ...` / `0 ...` |
| 64-byte label inside a ≤255-byte domain (`a`*64 + `.com`) | `1 0 1 0` — **domain does NOT check per-label length** |
| 127×`ü` (254 B) / 128×`ü` (256 B) | domain `1` / `0` (byte-based too) |

## Inferred rules (for this scope — entirely byte-level, no IDNA/punycode logic)

- `is_valid_domain(s)` = `!s.empty() && s.len() (bytes) <= 255`. No per-label length, dot, hyphen, or character-class checks.
- `is_valid_label(s)` = `!s.empty() && s.len() (bytes) <= 63`. Dots and every byte value count; a multi-label string is just measured as one blob.
- `is_ascii_domain(s)` = all bytes `< 0x80` (vacuously true for empty).
- `is_idn_domain(s)` = at least one byte `>= 0x80`. UTF-8 validity is irrelevant (raw `0xFF`/`0x80` count as IDN).
- `xn--` prefixes (any case) receive **zero special treatment**: no decode attempt, no decodability check, and they don't flip `is_idn_domain`. Uppercase punycode is indistinguishable from any ASCII. The four outputs are mutually consistent: `ascii XOR idn` always (since any string is either all-ASCII or has a non-ASCII byte), and `valid_label ⇒ valid_domain` except trivially.
